connections.note: The UAlbany News Center release of 4 June 2025 states: 'Utilizing a diverse set of devices to capture different types of data on many channels, UAlbany authors Matthew Szydagis, Kevin Knuth and Cecilia Levy, along with Ben Kugielsky of UAPx, a non-profit scientific research organization, collected observable-light and infrared images during a field expedition in 2021 to Laguna Beach, California.' The release also records the outcome honestly - 'the UAlbany research team succeeded in plausibly explaining all but one of the potential anomalies detected' - and quotes Szydagis on the single unresolved ambiguity. A state university issuing a press release claiming a UAP field-instrumentation result as institutional output is the substantive reason this node belongs on the board.

desc: Published in Progress in Aerospace Sciences volume 156, article 101099, in June 2025 (DOI 10.1016/j.paerosci.2025.101099) by Matthew Szydagis, Kevin H. Knuth, Benjamin Kugielsky and Cecilia Levy. It reports the results of UAPx's first instrumented field expedition, conducted off Catalina Island, California, using multi-band optical and other sensors with explicit treatment of instrumental artefacts and false positives. Its significance is not any single detection but the fact that the field now has a published, mainstream-journal field protocol written by particle physicists - a baseline against which any future government-released sensor data can be compared, and a template that no government programme has ever put in the public domain.
